qt: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

In a recent interview1, European Chief Prosecutor Laura Codruța Kövesi made some very serious allegations, notably stating that the most blatant attempt at intimidating the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) was witnessed in Greece. The European Chief Prosecutor underlined the systematic difficulties, pressure and obstacles faced by the EPPO when investigating cases of corruption and financial fraud affecting the financial interests of the EU. These statements raise serious concerns about whether the principles of the rule of law are being upheld and about the independence of the judiciary and the effective protection of the European budget. Given that every participating Member State has a legal and institutional obligation to ensure the safe, full and unhindered operation of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, can the Commission say: 1.
What is its official position regarding the European Chief Prosecutor’s specific complaints about attempts to intimidate and obstruct the work of the EPPO?
What steps does it intend to take to ensure Member States’ full, unhindered and safe cooperation with the EPPO?

What specific measures does it intend to take to safeguard the independence of European investigating authorities and ensure that allegations of fraud involving European funds are investigated without political or other interference?
